entries.title: Test platform globals with the implementation shipped on the phone
entries.trigger: shared TypeScript uses AbortSignal or other Web globals in React Native and Node tests.
entries.mechanism: a pre-request `signal.throwIfAborted()` compiled and passed Node-based tests, but the pinned React Native AbortController polyfill did not implement that method. Every device request failed before HTTP; intentional silent failure handling concealed the defect from the UI.
entries.prevention: inspect the pinned runtime implementation before using a newer Web method. Use the supported `signal.aborted` property for cancellation guards; do not add a custom polyfill merely to match Node. A TypeScript declaration or MDN API listing does not prove native support.
verification: run the API regression with the actual polyfill resolved from React Native's package, including an aborted token lookup. Then confirm a real device request reaches the service. For silent writes, inspect the resulting persisted row, not only the lack of an error screen.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, React Native 0.86.3 using abort-controller 3.0.0. Recheck on runtime upgrades.

entries.title: Transport completion and native display are separate image phases
entries.trigger: a maintained native image view downloads, decodes, processes and presents large remote media while the application adds its own progress watchdog and signed-URL recovery.
entries.mechanism: one 15-second watchdog remained active until `onDisplay`. Expo Image could emit successful `onLoad` first, but the application still classified the later display delay as a URL failure. Repeating that synthetic failure suppressed a valid photo even though Storage returned HTTP 200; a later independent refetch made the same photo appear.
entries.prevention: stop the transport watchdog on native load completion but reserve visible readiness for `onDisplay`. A missing display callback is not an authorization or media error: keep the native view mounted, probe the stable disk key again and adopt an available prepared file. Enter URL recovery and terminal unavailable state only from a real native image error. If the prepared file itself fails, try the remote source before its bounded URL recovery. Do not infer an ordering between native load and display callbacks. Successful display is monotonic for the exact mounted source: a later start, load, progress, error or watchdog callback cannot rearm a deadline or downgrade it.
verification: reproduce `onLoad` before the watchdog deadline and delay `onDisplay` beyond it; assert no URL recovery, suppression or error placeholder and accept the late display. Separately prove a native `onDisplay` -> `onLoad` order, advance beyond every deadline and assert the photo remains loaded. Also prove a no-progress cache probe adopts `file://`, a broken file falls back to remote and repeated real remote errors remain bounded. Finish with the affected large photo on the physical device and weak network.
boundaries: 2026-09-12, Expo Image 57.0.4 and React 19.2. Source regressions pass; physical iOS, physical Android, and released-artifact acceptance remain separate.

entries.title: Virtualized media feeds need sparse observation and keyed readiness
entries.trigger: a long virtualized feed combines exact visibility accounting, bounded image preparation, reusable disk bytes and native decoded-image caching.
entries.mechanism: four mechanisms were initially confused. A frame-rate JS scroll callback repeatedly restarted view timers; global cache stores notified unrelated mounted consumers; a hidden full-size preview warmup retained native decoded references without explicit release; and the primary list reduced React Native's virtualization window far below its defaults. Whole blank rows were a list fill-rate failure, while loaders inside mounted rows were image-readiness or decoded-memory behavior. A small custom decoded-image keepalive then looked better for one short pass but thrashed during repeated reverse traversal, repeatedly decoding from disk while native heap and total RSS climbed. A cache below the active working set can be worse than no second cache.
entries.prevention: restore supported virtualization defaults before cache experiments. Use native list viewability only to shortlist rows; qualify exact displayed-photo geometry after movement stops. Publish readiness through key-scoped subscriptions, keep callbacks stable, retain bounded disk preparation and delay heavier preview decode until idle. Every explicitly created native `ImageRef` needs a width/height bound and explicit release for unmount, replacement and late completion. Do not layer a custom decoded LRU over the maintained image library without isolated repeated-scroll proof.
verification: distinguish absent cells, mounted placeholders, repeated image loads and missing pages. Prove no view records during movement and that the final fully visible shared item records only after a fresh idle dwell. On the affected device, test a cold first pass, immediate reverse, and repeated middle-list traversal with stable process identity, frame data, native heap, bitmap count/bytes, and a visual blank-row check. A good short pass cannot close a progressive regression.
boundaries: 2026-09-09, React Native 0.86.3, Expo Image 57.0.4, and React 19.2. Physical Android acceptance and a later controlled repeated-list traversal found no blank cells and no memory growth in that run. Longer datasets, iOS, and a production artifact remain separate evidence.

entries.title: Image loaders follow usable pixels, not request ownership
entries.trigger: several component instances or product surfaces render one logical image while URLs, dimensions, transforms or native cache state change independently.
entries.mechanism: image consumers treated local request settlement as presentation identity. A compact profile image could paint shimmer above cached pixels after a larger instance displayed the same version; detail, message, and editor remounts or layout changes could do the same. A passive effect could also reset settled state after a fast native callback.
entries.prevention: share account-scoped readiness by immutable entity/version key and treat native display as stronger evidence than a late cache probe. Keep a same-identity cached, local or displayed source exposed during technical refresh. For a real content replacement, retain the old source only as an underlying placeholder and cover it until the new source displays; failure must terminate loading and surface an explicit operation error before the old image returns. Do not retain decoded native image references globally, and do not count registry readiness as user-visible display.
verification: cross feed, map, and message surfaces with one entity key; display one profile-image size and mount another; rotate a signed URL, advance the profile-image version, replace editor files, change layout/transform, fail a replacement, and remove it. Delay the cache probe past display, then repeat after an account change. Inspect the rendered image and overlay, not only network completion.
boundaries: 2026-09-08, Expo Image 57.0.4 and React 19.2 with component and cache-boundary regressions. Physical iPhone lifecycle and reconnect acceptance remain separate.

entries.title: Native cleanup completion can be a value, not just a resolved promise
entries.trigger: a native deletion API resolves a success boolean; a durable reset marker is cleared only after local cleanup succeeds.
entries.mechanism: allSettled outcomes were discarded, including Android's documented false when no Activity is available. Reset then erased its retry marker without confirmed cache deletion.
entries.prevention: wait for entered cleanup operations and inspect their documented success values before clearing durable intent. Propagate failure through the existing recovery path. Treat account switching, anonymous-to-confirmed transfer, and account deletion as different operations; do not infer transfer semantics from a generic logout implementation without the product contract.
verification: inject false and rejection, including another still-pending cache operation; preserve the marker and retry successfully. Separately inspect real device caches after background/restart.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo Image 57.0.4 Android/iOS. Web deliberately reports false and requires its own supported cleanup contract; this rule must not blindly block a web logout.

entries.title: Native Map style identity includes localization inputs
entries.trigger: MapLibre Native views receive a language-transformed Style JSON from React Native while the native Map can remain mounted or reuse previously laid-out symbol labels.
entries.mechanism: with Russian selected, a physical test device first rendered English labels and changed them to Russian only after the first zoom. The JavaScript style query distinguished `en`/`ru`, but the native Map instance identity did not.
entries.prevention: include the effective language in both the style query and native Map identity, and mount the native view only after the localized style is ready. Preserve camera state independently.
verification: inspect the first settled frame before any gesture on a cold launch, then switch language on a retained route in both directions and again inspect before panning or zooming. Cover translated names, missing-translation local fallback and non-name labels. Expression tests alone do not prove native label-bucket replacement.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, MapLibre React Native 11.3.6, MapTiler Streets v4, Android a physical test device.

entries.title: Keep local camera files independent of remote image slots
entries.trigger: iOS image components and bounded decode helpers share SDWebImage's default loader.
entries.mechanism: an uncached file URL enters the same six-operation downloader as remote images. Six stalled remote jobs can block both local display and processing; a UI timeout does not remove that dependency, so the photo may appear minutes later when unrelated jobs finish.
entries.prevention: use the installed SDK's supported direct local-byte cache API before publishing the source, verify the disk entry, then use disk-capable consumers with the exact same key. Preserve bounded decoding and account cleanup ownership. Audit placeholders and subsequent processing consumers too; a memory-only view cannot consume the seeded disk entry. Do not disable unrelated background work or increase deadlines as a substitute for isolating the local path.
verification: hold all remote slots with a native protocol fixture, then require local preview and bounded processing to complete without releasing those jobs. Also cover producer-to-editor-to-save and stale completion after a retake action in application tests. First-session physical QA remains separate.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, Expo Image 57.0.4 and an SDWebImage 5.21-compatible iOS framework. The native baseline blocks and the seeded path completes with six jobs held. A tester accepted rapid camera entry and repeated retake actions on a clean development install; live queue occupancy was not measured on device. Revalidate on dependency upgrades.

entries.title: Bound post-camera image readiness before enabling recovery
entries.trigger: a system camera returns a local file that must render through a separate native image component before the application can reveal its framing UI.
entries.mechanism: the presentation wait ended only on one native display callback. When that callback did not arrive, progress had no terminal condition. Retake then invoked the camera from the same stale render whose transition flag was still active; its guard rejected the launch while the native-handoff ref remained set, leaving an opaque cover with no recovery.
entries.prevention: accept documented native load or display completion through one idempotent readiness boundary. Keep the fast path behind the existing camera cover, disclose progress only after a short delay, and enforce a user-visible deadline with Retry and Retake. A recovery that depends on cleared React state must commit that state first and let a focused post-render lifecycle launch the external activity; do not call a render-captured guarded launcher synchronously after state setters.
verification: suppress native display completion, exercise the deadline, retry the same local file, then use the retake action and require a second real system-camera launch. Also deliver load followed by display and prove readiness is published once. Use physical iOS and Android camera-return and retake checks because mocked callbacks do not establish native event order or external-activity presentation.

treat the presentation deadline as neither native cancellation nor diagnosis. Repeated failed retake actions followed by recovery on lock/unlock invalidate ordinary warm-session coverage. Preserve first-install, permission-grant, and lifecycle evidence; do not infer success from manually emitted image callbacks.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3, Expo SDK 57, Expo Image 57.0.4 and Expo ImagePicker 57.0.16. Focused regressions passed; a tester accepted ordinary photo return and Retake on physical iOS and Android devices. Production first-session acceptance was invalidated later the same day. The related native queue lesson records the reproduced boundary and repaired clean-development-install acceptance.

entries.title: Overscan an SVG scrim inside its clipped Android edge
entries.trigger: an absolutely positioned `react-native-svg` scrim ends exactly at the clipped edge of native photo media.
entries.mechanism: on Android, an exact bottom-aligned SVG left one physical pixel row of the photo uncovered. The row followed the photo colors across multiple images and appeared in both feed and map-sheet presentations; the same shared presentation had no separator at that edge and iPhone did not show it.
entries.prevention: scope the compensation to Android and move the bottom scrim beyond the parent clip by `StyleSheet.hairlineWidth`. Preserve the exact iOS position, gradient opacity, media size and controls.
verification: first capture two different photos and both shared presentation modes on the affected device. Add a platform regression for Android overscan and unchanged iOS placement, then reload the real bundle and inspect a nearest-neighbor crop of the final media row.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3 and react-native-svg 15.15.4. A physical Android 16 device reproduced the seam and verified its removal after a development-bundle reload.

entries.title: Parent opacity can expose fallback layers beneath native images
entries.trigger: a native image is intentionally layered above a fallback view, and an ancestor uses opacity to communicate transient state.
entries.mechanism: Android composited the complete subtree at reduced opacity, making the fallback icon visible through a custom profile image and changing the apparent bubble color. The same parent-alpha treatment looked acceptable on iOS, so cross-platform source symmetry hid the device defect.
entries.prevention: when the ancestor-opacity treatment is intentional, use the framework's supported offscreen alpha compositing on the affected platform so overlapping children are combined before alpha is applied. Bound any hardware texture to the active animation/state and release it afterward. If the compositing cost is not acceptable, move the visual treatment to a non-overlapping indicator rather than allowing platform-specific blending.
verification: render the pending and confirmed states under explicit Android and iOS platform values, assert the ancestor opacity and transition calls, then inspect a real custom image over its fallback on the affected device. Source tests cannot establish native compositor output.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3, Expo Image 57 and Reanimated 4.2.1. Android physical acceptance of the repair remains pending.

entries.title: Serialize application-owned native modal presentation through dismissal
entries.trigger: multiple retained screens or global providers can independently request React Native modal presentation, including a modal opened as a follow-up to another sheet action.
entries.mechanism: an iPhone post-share rationale and a map detail sheet entered on independent timelines; the later sheet covered the rationale and left the screen blocked. React Native iOS keeps a modal rendered until its native dismissal callback, while native host presentation and dismissal are asynchronous.
entries.prevention: give application-owned React Native modals one presentation owner. Queue later requests, cancel requests whose retained screen loses focus, and release the active slot from native `onDismiss`, not from the start or JS-animation end of a close. Run follow-up actions and navigation only after that callback. Route-driven attached surfaces wait for an existing native modal; an intentional modal over an attached sheet starts only after that sheet's entrance completion.
verification: prove a second modal stays unmounted after the first becomes logically hidden and is granted only after the first native dismissal callback. Cover cancellation before grant, route focus loss and the real producer-to-consumer sequence. Physical iOS acceptance must confirm touch recovery.
boundaries: 2026-09-13, React Native 0.86.3. Source regressions pass; a tester accepted the repaired behavior on clean Android and iPhone development installs.

entries.title: Keep cache-hit work behind native transition boundaries
entries.trigger: a native sheet or overlay has lightweight entrance chrome and can reveal a cached, render-heavy presentation after it becomes visible.
entries.mechanism: hiding cached content until entrance completion still forced a visible skeleton for every repeat, while mounting the complete cached native image tree on tap could delay the first frame. Populated close and a concurrent map-camera transition both stepped even when timing was assigned first.
entries.prevention: do not retain a dismissed full-screen native overlay as a content cache. Remove it from the native hierarchy, retain only query data, layout results and the platform image cache, and rebuild the visible surface from those stores. Use the lightweight shell for unretained content. Never overlap an expensive native owner transition with the overlay exit merely because both have UI-thread timing. Keep presentation-only camera changes out of semantic viewport/query state. Do not rasterize a large, image-rich iOS surface for repeated motion without physical memory/GPU evidence: cached repetitions can become progressively slower even when the first cycle improves. A narrow platform-specific core native-driver path is preferable when it isolates only the failing programmatic transition.
verification: prove the dismissed overlay is absent, the last ready identity reopens from data/layout and image cache without another shell, the map camera starts only after completed dismissal, presentation camera events do not publish query state, and repeated cached cycles do not degrade. Physical marker hit testing and frame pacing still require each device.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3 / Reanimated 4.5.1 / Expo Image 57.0.4. Source regressions pass; a tester accepted repeated cold and cached cycles on a physical device after rasterization removal, native-driver isolation, and presentation-viewport suppression.

entries.title: Preserve inseparable share copy as one activity item
entries.trigger: a system Share Sheet must deliver multiple pieces of text together, such as an introduction followed by a public URL.
entries.mechanism: React Native passed iOS `message` and `url` as separate activity items. A physical iPhone target accepted only the URL, so the required localized introduction disappeared even though the JavaScript payload contained both fields.
entries.prevention: when both pieces are required and editable, combine them into one `message` string. Use a separate URL item only when independent target selection is acceptable. Preserve platform-only subject or chooser options separately.
verification: assert the exact single-item payload, then share to real iOS targets and confirm the composed text remains editable. A mocked `Share.share` call does not prove target-extension behavior.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3 Share implementation and tester-reported physical iPhone failure. Post-fix physical acceptance remains required.

entries.title: Bound native image decode before manipulation
entries.trigger: a platform camera can return a JPEG whose decoded pixel buffer is far larger than its compressed file, including 200 MP and future higher-resolution sensors.
entries.mechanism: the capture flow passed the original URI directly to ImageManipulator while the framing flow also rendered that URI with downscaling disabled. Android therefore could decode one or more full-size bitmaps before the requested resize. A tester-reported 200 MP path terminated the application; repeated first-attempt failures on a 12 MP Android path are consistent with the same overlapping decode pressure, but that exact production exception was not persisted.
entries.prevention: retain/copy the accepted camera file unchanged for explicit product uses such as gallery export, but load a dimension-bounded native ImageRef before manipulation. Pass that bounded reference to the native manipulator, allow the visible editor to downscale to its view, release every context and image reference, and reduce output dimensions as well as quality when a byte ceiling cannot be met.
verification: use real camera files at ordinary and maximum sensor settings, confirm that the framing flow succeeds on the first attempt and the process survives, inspect derived dimensions/bytes, and separately prove untouched gallery export. Keep client, hosted validator and restored-media limits compatible before release.
boundaries: 2026-09-10, Expo Image 57.0.4 and ImageManipulator 57.0.16. a physical test device ordinary-camera smoke passed; Samsung 200 MP acceptance remains required after release.

entries.title: An application deadline must stop owned native work
entries.trigger: a native one-shot operation can outlive a JavaScript timeout and the API exposes no per-request cancellation handle.
entries.mechanism: the application deadline returned `null` and released single-flight ownership while iOS `getCurrentPositionAsync` could remain pending. Retry could start a second native request even though the expired request still owned Core Location work.
entries.prevention: use a maintained scoped subscription when its removal is the supported cancellation mechanism. Treat the subscription capability as part of request deduplication. Remove it on success, native error and deadline; if registration resolves after cancellation, remove it immediately. Reject callbacks from expired ownership before publishing state.
verification: deadline before and after subscription registration, late callback, Retry success and compatible concurrent callers. Preserve the unaffected platform path explicitly. Native cancellation still requires device evidence under a real unavailable-provider condition.
boundaries: 2026-09-10, Expo Location 57.0.16 / iOS Core Location. Android one-shot acquisition remains outside this repair.

entries.title: Verify the platform event sequence before adding an interaction guard
entries.trigger: a Pressable supports both a tap and a long press.
entries.mechanism: a manual flag expected onPress after onLongPress to clear itself. Native Pressability suppresses that onPress, so the flag instead swallowed the next independent tap.
entries.prevention: use the platform's existing tap/long-press separation. Avoid a second event state machine unless a reproduced unsupported interaction requires it.
verification: use full press/long-press sequences, release, then a new tap. A test that manually emits the suppressed event can validate the wrong behavior. Separately check native modal return and gesture arbitration on each supported platform.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, React Native 0.86.3 Pressability and RNTL 14 userEvent regressions.

entries.title: Gesture activation and successful completion are different boundaries
entries.trigger: a native gesture takes ownership of an animation or commits a dismiss/action.
entries.mechanism: begin callbacks can precede recognition and never receive an active-end callback; active-end callbacks can also represent cancellation. Cancelling motion on mere touch can freeze it, while ignoring completion status can commit an interrupted action.
entries.prevention: use the installed library's activation callback to take animation ownership. Commit only on successful completion and restore cancelled active interaction through the existing path.
verification: touch without activation during entry, short drag, completed threshold drag, system cancellation beyond the threshold, reduced motion and a subsequent normal action. Callback tests verify application branching; real gesture arbitration and animation require native evidence.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Gesture Handler 2.32.0 dispatch and component regressions. Version 3 uses a different callback contract; recheck on upgrade. Physical system cancellation remains separate.

entries.title: Recover external results only with their originating context
entries.trigger: Android destroys the Activity while a system camera or media picker is open.
entries.mechanism: the original JavaScript promise and volatile screen state may be lost, while the native module retains a pending result shared by multiple application features.
entries.prevention: inspect the supported pending-result API and bind recovery to durable initiating context before adoption. Do not assign an unidentified result to whichever account/route is current. Decide explicitly whether an unsaved draft is recoverable; do not invent missing location or owner.
verification: use Android's Don't keep activities and actual memory pressure; exercise camera, profile-image picker, cancellation, and account changes. Check ownership and timestamps after restart.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo ImagePicker 57 documents getPendingResultAsync; native behavior remains device-dependent. The missing-consumer diagnosis is separate from physical reproduction.

entries.title: Embedded content has a separate process lifetime
entries.trigger: a native WebView hosts an authentication/security challenge or another required step.
entries.mechanism: OS termination stops content callbacks. A timer disabled during user interaction cannot later detect the dead renderer, leaving the step without recovery controls.
entries.prevention: handle the maintained WebView's platform termination callbacks through the existing retry/cancel state. A fresh attempt must replace the dead instance and reject stale results.
verification: deliver Android/iOS termination events during interaction, retry and accept only the new result. Separately exercise real memory pressure/background and native process termination.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, react-native-webview 13.16.1 props and callback regressions; physical proof pending.

entries.title: Scope gesture workarounds to the affected platform
entries.trigger: a core Pressable is replaced with a library/native button to repair tap arbitration.
entries.mechanism: an iOS first-tap fix also selected RNGH's Android NativeButton, whose rounded background did not clip a child gradient image. Other CTAs using the core RN view clipped normally.
entries.prevention: apply a platform-specific workaround only where needed. Verify visual child clipping as well as touch delivery when changing the native host component; prop similarity is insufficient. Give gradient children an explicit rounded clipping View when their touch host does not own clipping.
verification: inspect the real affected platform, normal/disabled/loading states and first tap with and without the keyboard. Mocked Pressable tests cannot prove native masking or hit testing.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, RNGH 2.32.0 / RN 0.86.3; an Android screenshot and installed native source confirm the mismatch. Platform scoping alone did not meet acceptance; an explicit child clipping layer was added. Action regressions pass and a tester subsequently confirmed normal Android button appearance. Separate iOS keyboard/tap behavior was preserved by the narrow platform scope.

entries.title: Reconcile keyboard scroll and safe area with the final viewport
entries.trigger: a focused multiline input lives in a ScrollView above a fixed footer while `KeyboardAvoidingView` changes the usable viewport on iOS or Android.
entries.mechanism: `keyboardDidShow` can request `scrollToEnd` before the resized viewport finishes its layout. The scroll is correct for the earlier height but still leaves a counter or lower field edge behind the footer after settling. On iOS, keeping the persistent bottom safe area inside padding-based keyboard avoidance also reserves the home-indicator space twice and moves the footer unnecessarily far above a docked keyboard.
entries.prevention: keep the keyboard-event scroll, then coalesce one more focused-input scroll from the ScrollView layout while the keyboard is visible. On iOS, place the safe-area wrapper outside keyboard avoidance so its measured frame excludes the persistent bottom inset; preserve the accepted Android height/adjustResize structure.
verification: ignore screenshots captured during keyboard motion. Wait for the keyboard and viewport to settle, then require the full editor, counter, ordinary spacing and fixed action to be visible together on physical devices for both affected platforms and compact screen heights.
boundaries: 2026-09-11, React Native 0.86.3 / Expo SDK 57. A physical Android test accepted the repair; a tester-provided iPhone screenshot confirmed the iOS failure, focused source regressions pass, and physical iPhone acceptance of the replacement remains pending.

entries.title: Let handled controls receive the first touch above an open keyboard
entries.trigger: interactive children such as message actions live inside a ScrollView or FlatList while a sibling TextInput owns a dismissible software keyboard.
entries.mechanism: React Native's default `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="never"` captures the first non-input touch and withholds it from descendants so the touch only blurs the input. A long press therefore requires a second gesture even though the child Pressable is otherwise correct.
entries.prevention: use `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` when handled child controls should act on the first touch while unhandled list taps may still dismiss the keyboard. On Android, do not promise that a normal same-window app overlay can cover the retained system IME: it remains below that system window, while a React Native Modal can remove the underlying input's window focus. When the action must occupy the keyboard area, explicitly dismiss the keyboard and open the modal in the same child callback so the user still performs only one gesture.
verification: assert the list responder configuration and the child action/draft transition in source tests, then verify the original first-touch sequence and overlay geometry with the real keyboard on every supported physical platform. A mocked long press cannot prove native responder arbitration.
boundaries: 2026-09-12, React Native 0.86.3 / Expo SDK 57. The installed ScrollView source and a failing message-surface regression confirmed the default capture path. Android physical evidence showed that Modal dismissed the keyboard and the same-window alternative remained below the IME with partial lower occlusion. The final one-callback dismissal plus modal path passes source tests and received physical acceptance on iPhone and Android.

entries.title: Autolinking does not apply config plugins to an existing native project
entries.trigger: installing a native module whose generated resource controls runtime behavior.
entries.mechanism: Expo run reuses an existing native directory, Gradle links the newly installed module, and a missing app resource leaves the module's own default active. A correct clean prebuild elsewhere does not repair that existing project.
entries.prevention: regenerate the affected working native project after plugin/module changes, preserving intentional local overrides, then rebuild. Check source generation and compiled settings separately.
verification: compare OS state, compiled resource and actual app behavior before/after; install over the current development app without resetting data. Retain separate signed release acceptance.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo CLI 57.0.22/SystemUI 57.0.3, Android. SystemUI defaults to light unless its generated resource selects automatic. This is not a reason to replace supported Appearance hooks.
